Now I have a thorough picture of both the advisory and the existing rule framework. Here are two proposed deterministic pre-filter rules:

---

## Two Proposed Deterministic Pre-Filter Rules

These are purely mechanical checks — no AI judgement required, just a grep or a byte scan — that would have flagged `fast-pay-utils@2.1.0` before any human or agent reviewed its code.

---

### Rule 1 — Unicode Tags-block characters in published file content

**Check:** Scan every file in the installed package tree (or tarball) for any codepoint in the range U+E0000–U+E007F. Emit a finding if one is present.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Rationale** | The entire Unicode Tags block has no legitimate use in source code or documentation; its only known application in published packages is invisible prompt-injection payload delivery. |
| **ASI Category** | **ASI01** — Agent Goal Hijack |
| **CWE** | **CWE-829** — Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere |

This rule would have fired the moment the `README.md` or [`src/index.ts`](packages/fast-pay-utils/2.1.0/src/index.ts) was unpacked, before any agent or developer read a single line.

---

### Rule 2 — Anomalous maximum line length in source files (indentation-obfuscation heuristic)

**Check:** For every `.js`, `.ts`, `.mjs`, or `.cjs` file in the package, compute the length of the longest line. If that length exceeds a threshold (e.g. 300 characters) and the excess is composed predominantly of whitespace followed by code, emit a finding.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| **Rationale** | Legitimate source code has no reason to push statements ~300 spaces to the right; such extreme leading-whitespace indentation is a documented obfuscation technique used specifically to hide malicious statements from casual diff and editor scrolling. |
| **ASI Category** | **ASI05** — Unexpected Code Execution (RCE) |
| **CWE** | **CWE-506** — Embedded Malicious Code |

The `dynamicRequire` / `netClient` block in [`src/index.ts`](packages/fast-pay-utils/2.1.0/src/index.ts:137) has lines exceeding 300 leading spaces; a trivial `awk 'length > 300'` pass over any `.ts` file in the tarball would have surfaced it immediately.

---

### Why these are genuinely deterministic

Both checks are **byte-level or character-count operations** with no model inference:

- Rule 1 is a single `python3` range test on each character (the advisory itself already shows exactly this script in the Remediation section).
- Rule 2 is a one-liner: `awk '{ if (length($0) > 300 && $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]{200,}/) print FILENAME, NR, length($0) }'`.

Neither requires understanding what the code *does* — they flag structural anomalies that are near-zero-false-positive indicators of the two specific techniques (`fast-pay-utils@2.1.0` used both).
